entities.summary: Sir Vincent Arthur Henry McMahon was a British Indian Army officer and diplomat who served as Foreign Secretary in the Government of India from 1911 to 1915 and as High Commissioner in Egypt from 1915 to 1917. As the Foreign Secretary McMahon conducted the tripartite negotiations between Tibet, China and Britain that led to the Simla Convention. Even though China did not in the end sign the Convention, the agreement governed the British relations with Tibet till 1947. In Egypt, McMahon was best known for the McMahon-Hussein Correspondence with Hussein bin Ali, Sharif of Mecca, and the Declaration to the Seven in response to a memorandum written by seven notable Syrians.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The McMahon-Hussein Correspondence led to the partition of Ottoman territories in the Middle East and had significant regional implications for the modern Middle East. The Simla Convention also governed British relations with Tibet until 1947.
